description_full: Aura Minerals Inc., a gold and copper production company, focuses on the development and operation of gold and base metal projects in the Americas. It operates through The Minosa Mine, The Apoena Mine, the Aranzazu Mine, The Almas Mine, and The Borborema Mine and the Serra Grande Mine Projects segments. The company primarily explores gold, copper, and silver deposits. The company was formerly known as Aura Gold Inc. and changed its name to Aura Minerals Inc. in July 2007. The company was incorporated in 1946 and is headquartered in Coconut Grove, Florida.
ceo_bio: Mr. Rodrigo Cardoso Barbosa | CEO & President | Age 51 | Compensation: $1.7M (FY2024)
financial_summary: Aura Minerals Inc. is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $6.5B market cap on $922M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +33% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +9.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 19% against a 10% cost of capital — a 9-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 37%.
The business throws off $126M in free cash flow — roughly 14 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
Accruals are elevated at -23.9% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.3× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 15× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 1.3% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 51% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 49% operating margin runs 40pp above the Basic Materials median (10%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.04 across 219 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 169% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 29% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 77% and a beta of 1.08, it moves roughly with the market.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $61.70 (margin of safety -26%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 0%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $28.01 to $132 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Basic Materials peers: P/E 22.0 vs 16.5 and P/FCF 51.9 vs 22.8 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 1.9% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 7.3% (vs the 8% bar).
The 10 covering analysts target $103 on average, 32% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 25.0% annual cash-flow growth, 4pp more than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 19% clears the cost of capital of 9.7% by 9pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.72).
It runs a 37% gross margin and converts 14% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is a concern: cash conversion of only -3.85x and high accruals (-23.9% of assets).
SG&A jumped 58% last year, worth watching.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.3x net debt to EBITDA ($286.1M of cash against $435.3M of debt), with interest covered 15.1x.
Warning signs: a Beneish M-score that flags possible earnings manipulation, which caps the rating at HOLD.

growth: Revenue has compounded at 32.9% over 3 years.

It has missed earnings estimates by 24.4% on average.

Insiders have only sold over the past year (7 sales, net $26.7M sold).

Short interest is elevated at 16.2% of the float, 5.4 days to cover.
